nodes.label: s1: dice tumble
nodes.rationale: Faces flip through Simulation 1's first 15 logged rolls and land on the near miss [4, 4, 4, 5, 4] at the 1.60 s beat with the odd die outlined red; real rolls instead of Math.random keep the render deterministic.

nodes.label: yc-parody tone preset
nodes.rationale: Hard cuts, one claim per beat and zero jokes in the copy; the corporate-warm bed and lab-report seriousness make the dice statistics funny on their own.

nodes.label: /hyperframes skill router
nodes.rationale: Skills encode framework-specific patterns (window.__timelines registration, data-* semantics, shader-compatible CSS) missing from generic web docs; skipping them produces broken compositions.

nodes.label: Beat grid and strong cues (114.84 BPM)
nodes.norm_label: beat grid and strong cues (114.84 bpm)

nodes.label: /brag workflow
nodes.rationale: /brag runs as its own workflow, skipping the hyperframes entry-point interview and the generic promo workflow.

nodes.label: Motion-matched sparse SFX
nodes.rationale: At most seven cue moments, each matched to an on-screen gesture (dice, keys, counter lock, spike, stamp, logo bell); no SFX under readable headlines or on every terminal line, and nothing louder than the bed except the hook dice and the logo hit.

nodes.label: Music cue locks (6.34 / 9.50 / 12.65 s)
nodes.rationale: At most three hard locks (terminal cut-in, counter lock, 8,738 callout) with other cues as soft bias; cues bias timing but never drive visible pulsing, and there is no audio-reactive treatment because stillness sells the seriousness.

nodes.label: Serious science for stupid questions
nodes.rationale: The comedy is the gap between a silly question and absurd rigor, so the film plays it straight: every number is real and the numbers are the jokes.

nodes.label: Agent-safe background preview
nodes.rationale: A run_in_background wrapper around npm run dev stays owned by the invoking session and can vanish while the browser stays open, so agents use npx hyperframes preview --background and stop it explicitly.

nodes.label: Pinned hyperframes CLI version
nodes.rationale: Scripts pin an exact hyperframes@X.Y.Z so the project re-renders identically over time; upgrades go through npx hyperframes@latest upgrade.

nodes.label: Timed clip rule (data-start + .clip)
nodes.rationale: data-start is what marks an element as timed and the shared .clip CSS gives a scene its full-frame box; data-track-index is only a Studio display lane.

nodes.label: Cue use policy
nodes.rationale: Cues are optional hints: major reveals may move toward a strong cue within about 0.15 s and smaller entrances within about 0.10 s, and cues are ignored when they harm story, readability or pacing.

nodes.label: Music bed volume lane
nodes.rationale: The bed sits near 0.30 through a data-automation volume lane with a short fade-in and a fade to 0 by 23.0 s; no ducking is needed because there is no voice.

nodes.label: Video and GIF rebuild
nodes.rationale: GitHub's file viewer won't play the MP4 inline, so the README embeds a GIF that links to the raw MP4; ffmpeg -ss 0.0334 skips frame 0, where the poster image is baked in.

nodes.label: Lab-paper design tokens
nodes.rationale: STIX Two Math is loaded as a companion font because STIX Two Text lacks ≠ and ✓.

nodes.label: s4: seismograph chart
nodes.rationale: A linear y-axis (max 9,000) across all 200 runs lets the 8,738 spike tower over the dashed 1,296 line, revealed left to right at constant speed like a seismograph.

nodes.label: charts.ipynb
nodes.rationale: Separates data generation (main.py) from analysis and intuition building: regex-parses logs into a pandas DataFrame for histogram, volatility line, boxplot and cap-hit scatter plots.

nodes.label: 3 dice × 20 simulations run
nodes.rationale: Header reads 'Matrix size: 10 x 10' where the current main.py writes 'Columns per row: 10', so this log came from an earlier version of the script.

nodes.label: brainfarts-and-benchmarks
nodes.rationale: Small curiosity-driven questions would otherwise disappear; each one ends as runnable code plus a write-up of what was tested and learned.

nodes.label: share-copy-variants.md
nodes.rationale: Alternate captions in the same deadpan register as the canonical one, using only numbers from the repo's logs or test output.

nodes.label: STIX Two Text + IBM Plex Mono typography
nodes.norm_label: stix two text + ibm plex mono typography
nodes.rationale: STIX Two Text is the scientific-journal typeface, so headlines read like a paper title; it replaced IBM Plex Sans, which is not bundled, and journal serif plus instrument mono is a stronger register switch.

nodes.label: Seaborn whitegrid visual identity
nodes.rationale: The repo has no CSS, so the palette comes from its seaborn whitegrid notebook charts and terminal; the notebook's #FF0000 reference line becomes matplotlib tab:red #D62728 to pass WCAG AA as text.

nodes.label: Verbatim on-screen copy
nodes.rationale: No invented numbers or claims: every on-screen figure and quote comes from the logs, notebook, README, explained.md or pytest output.

nodes.label: Expected iterations 6^(n−1)
nodes.rationale: A single roll matches with probability 6 × (1/6)^n = 1/6^(n−1), so the expected count explodes with n: 1, 6, 36, 216, 1,296 for five dice, about 10 million for ten.

nodes.label: Geometric distribution
nodes.rationale: Iterations until a match are geometric: long right tails, large max/min gaps and unstable averages for small sample sizes.

nodes.label: Measure, don't assume
nodes.rationale: Claims come from runs, logs and tests, not intuition.

nodes.label: Playground, not a library
nodes.rationale: Not production code, a framework or a tutorial: a place to ask small questions in public and keep the answers. Tagline: 'If something here looks dumb — that's probably the point.'

nodes.label: Show the work
nodes.rationale: Every experiment ships an explained.md with the method, the numbers and the takeaway.

nodes.label: Same result ≠ same cost
nodes.rationale: Both approaches are O(n) in time and space; the gap is constant factors, so Big-O ≠ real-world performance.

nodes.label: Crossover: nums + nums wins for n ≤ 5, nums * 2 wins from n = 10
nodes.norm_label: crossover: nums + nums wins for n ≤ 5, nums * 2 wins from n = 10
nodes.rationale: Shown only in the table's winner column; the headline '0.105 µs faster' is the n = 100 result and does not hold for n ≤ 5.

nodes.label: list * 2 vs list + list experiment
nodes.rationale: Built to understand how identical results can have different costs, build intuition about Python internals and practice robust tests without overengineering.

nodes.label: pytest -q -s visible-case timing table (avg µs per call, 220 passed)
nodes.norm_label: pytest -q -s visible-case timing table (avg μs per call, 220 passed)

nodes.label: CPython single allocation for list * 2
nodes.rationale: list * 2 knows the final size, allocates once and copies references in a tight loop, while list + list builds its result with slightly more overhead.

nodes.label: sys.getsizeof container check
nodes.rationale: getsizeof measures only the list container, not the elements, so it only sanity-checks that output grows with input; true space reasoning stays conceptual O(n).

nodes.label: s3: terminal run + roll counter
nodes.rationale: The terminal card's opacity snaps in because a slow fade turns the dark card muddy gray over the paper; the counter is the running sum of the 200 real iteration counts, locking on the 9.50 s cue.

nodes.norm_label: how long until five dice match?

nodes.label: Dice matching experiment
nodes.rationale: Built to develop intuition about randomness: observe exponential probability effects, visualize variance and outliers, and practice logging and post-analysis.

nodes.label: Roll 15 near miss [4, 4, 4, 5, 4], no match
nodes.rationale: Five pip-drawn dice show four 4s and a single 5; the lone mismatched die is outlined in red and the roll counter (15) sits above a red 'no match' status, dramatizing how close a roll can get while the all-faces-equal condition still fails.

nodes.label: Per-run log file format
nodes.rationale: Each run writes {num_dice}die_{num_runs}sim_{date_time}.txt with metadata, every roll and the matching iteration, so runs are auditable, debuggable and re-analyzable.

nodes.label: Observability over efficiency
nodes.rationale: Intentionally inefficient but transparent: logging every roll costs O(n × k) time and unbounded log size, accepted because the goal is seeing randomness, not speed.

nodes.label: GSAP
nodes.rationale: GSAP 3.14.2 is vendored from the npm registry so rendering needs no CDN fetch.

nodes.label: Deterministic logic only
nodes.rationale: Renders must reproduce frame by frame, so no Date.now(), no Math.random() and no network fetches.

nodes.label: Paused root timeline on window.__timelines
nodes.rationale: The runtime seeks one registered paused root timeline; child scene timelines must not be paused, because a paused child does not advance when the root is seeked.

nodes.label: Registry catalog search
nodes.rationale: terminal-simulator, mk-line-graph and count-up were inspected, but none matched the exact repo output or a 200-point plot and no dice primitive exists, so the terminal, chart, counter and dice were hand-built.

nodes.label: Deterministic tl.set frame rows
nodes.rationale: Dice faces, counter digits and the terminal stream are set with tl.set rows (the registry count-up idiom) so every seek is deterministic without update callbacks.

nodes.label: s5: pytest summary terminal
nodes.rationale: The 0.105 µs stamp uses natural timing instead of the 17.91 s cue so it holds at least a second before the cut.

nodes.label: Adding an experiment
nodes.rationale: Name the folder after the question (snake_case when pytest must import it as a package, hence why_is_list_multiply_faster/__init__.py), keep code self-contained, write explained.md in the shared shape, assert correctness and average repeated timings, then add a row to the Experiments table.

nodes.label: Assert correctness, report speed
nodes.rationale: Timings depend on the machine and Python version, so benchmarks never fail a test for being slow; numbers are reported, never asserted.

nodes.label: One question per folder
nodes.rationale: Experiments stay self-contained, with no shared code between them.

nodes.label: Averaged timing (5,000 repeats)
nodes.rationale: Averaging 5,000 calls per method and never asserting on time avoids timing a single call or requiring one method to always win.

nodes.label: Call overhead dominates tiny lists
nodes.rationale: For n = 0..5, function-call and loop overhead plus CPU noise dominate, so results flip and plus can win; the list-copy cost only dominates for larger inputs.

nodes.label: LeetCode-style visible/hidden cases
nodes.rationale: Only n = 0, 1, 2, 5, 10, 50, 100 are timed and printed; the other 94 sizes run silently as hidden correctness cases, keeping output readable.

nodes.rationale: The 200-run mean (1,287.6) lands near the theoretical 1,296, yet single runs span 2 to 8,738 rolls, so the expected value says little about any one run.
